B. subtilis QueE converted CPH4 to CDG in the mixed-species reconstruction; the cloned and assayed QueE was Bacillus, not the E. coli expression host.
For B. subtilis QueE, product formed in 15-fold excess over supplied SAM, demonstrating regeneration of the cofactor rather than stoichiometric consumption.
The current reviewed net RHEA:27982 reaction and physiological RHEA:27983 direction consume two ATP and yield two AMP plus two diphosphate, assigned with ECO:0000255 HAMAP-Rule MF_01633.
Plasmid-borne queC restored Q modification in E. coli B105; mutant analyses place QueC before preQ0, providing genetic evidence rather than a purified E. coli enzyme assay.
Streptomyces rimosus ToyM activates CDG and the amide intermediate through two ATP-dependent half-reactions; AMP and pyrophosphate are produced with both substrates.
The entry annotates zinc-binding sites at residues 111, 114 and 182 with explicit ChEBI:29105 ligand cross-references.
The native enzyme comment identifies a catalytically active zinc ion; cited residue numbering differs by one from the current UniProt sequence.
QueD binds one zinc per subunit, with ECO:0000269 support from PMID:19231875, PMID:24816091 and PMID:24990950.

source_assertion_exclusions.disposition: Four mechanistic component reactions85175/85179/85183/85187 document the current two-adenylation mechanism; the chosen net27983 covers the complete transformation, so components are not additionally counted.
Sepiapterin/pyruvoyltetrahydropterin alternative substrate activities are outside the defined GTP route.
Inferred E. coli homodimer retained in functional-role prose; no externally issued E. coli complex identity was verified and no independent monomer sufficiency asserted.
E. coli FldA/FPR used with Bacillus QueE are assay activation machinery, not established physiological electron donors for E. coli QueE. No net donor or cofactor-FAD substitution invented.
QueF, Tgt, QueA, QueG/H and transport are distinct downstream processes; source defects and incomplete map do not close their discovery work.
Regulatory compounds outside the exact biosynthetic mechanism are not added; no claim that all FolE regulation is represented.
